Friction: Buyers compare these tools on price per article, but the vendors meter different units — Outrank bills articles, Arvow bills credits, RightBlogger bills sites and reports — so the cheapest-looking row is usually the one whose unit does the least work.
Logic: Outrank bundles three separable jobs (keyword research, drafting, scheduled publishing) behind one subscription, and most buyers only want one of them replaced. Sorting candidates by which job they refuse to do beats sorting by price. The trade-off worth naming: the bundled backlink-exchange feature both Outrank and RightBlogger ship sits directly against Google's link spam policy, and the 30-90 posts/month volume sits inside the range where scaled-content-abuse judgements get made — neither is the vendor's risk to carry.
content_angle: Work out which of the three bundled jobs you are actually replacing before comparing anything. Names our own gap out loud: we do not generate or publish articles, so if the 30-a-month output is why you subscribed, nothing on our side replaces it. Prices are quoted from each vendor's own pricing page with a verification date, and promotional rates are separated from regular ones.
